notes:
NDM 2.3.5 is a hardening release. It comes out of a full independent re-review of the 2.3.4 code base — every subsystem re-read, every fix from the previous round re-tested — and it closes what that review found, including one fix of our own that had never actually run.

The in-page download card now genuinely follows a download that was queued while the app was closed: the code that adopts the real entry id sat behind an early return and never executed, so the card stayed frozen while the download ran without it. A refusal from the app now fails the card with the reason shown, and a duplicate file download gets the "Already in NDM" answer instead of a phantom progress card tracking somebody else's download. On Facebook, a video object is only ever keyed by its own identity — an unidentified object can no longer borrow the page's video id and offer the wrong streams — and a WebM-only top quality is labelled WEBM, not MP4.

FTP downloads that cannot ask the server for a file size now require the server's completion reply before the file is called finished; a transfer the server aborts mid-way is an error with its resume data kept, not a silently truncated "success". A pasted FTP address with non-ASCII characters can no longer crash the add flow, FTP passwords stay out of the resume journal on every path (restart and Refresh Address included), and a class of FTP resume and error-classification bugs is closed. Video downloads are protected against a second engine starting over the first during the merge window, pausing a yt-dlp download now also stops the merge process it spawned, and two jobs racing for the same file name can no longer overwrite each other's streams.

The update feed itself is stronger on both ends: the app now consults every feed route and takes the highest version on offer, so one stale mirror can no longer make a newer release invisible, and the feed file is generated and verified by CI from the release's own artifacts instead of being attached by hand. On Linux, the date column can no longer lose its year at ordinary window sizes, an empty speed-limit field is refused instead of quietly becoming 512 KB/s, Resume stays greyed out on a finished download, and restarting after an update waits for the old instance to hand over instead of occasionally leaving no app running. On Windows, the main list's block map paints each download's real progress (the placeholder strip is gone), files can be dropped onto the Basket again, and long settings values are no longer cut off when Options is saved. Uninstalling the Linux package now also removes the browser host registrations it created.
